device.category: 8-voice analogue polyphonic synthesizer with program memory, desktop / Eurorack (80 HP)
device.based_on: Sequential Circuits Prophet-600, extended from 6 to 8 voices, running a firmware descended from GliGli's open-source Prophet-600 remake (Behringer's launch material says it includes all the GliGli modifications). The guide names neither; large parts of its text are copied from the GliGli manual.

sources.title: PRO-800 Quick Start Guide
sources.note: 62 numbered controls (the English control list is typeset out of order and several numbers are unreadable), an additional parameters table, global settings and preset tables, keyboard modes, arpeggiator and sequencer procedures, a MIDI CC map and a specifications table.

sources.title: PRO-800 front panel photograph
sources.note: Used to place the controls the numbered list garbles, and for LED colours.

sources.title: GliGli's Sequential Circuits Prophet 600 Firmware Upgrade, Release 2.0 (user manual)
sources.note: Manual for the open-source Prophet-600 CPU and firmware remake. Much of the PRO-800 guide's text (tune routine, keyboard modes, voice priority, LFO shape procedure, oscillator pot modes) is copied from it with the voice count changed from 6 to 8.

sources.title: gligli/p600fw source code (GitHub), version 2.1 RC3, last GliGli commit September 2015
sources.note: Envelope and LFO code read directly: envelopes are Electric Druid ENVGEN7-derived DDS generators updated at 2 kHz per voice; the LFO is exponential-rate DDS at 2 kHz. Stage times and LFO range below are computed from its lookup tables.

sources.title: image-et-son/p600fw (Imogen's continuation of GliGli, v2022)
sources.note: Adds a 'vintage' spread parameter that offsets pitch and envelope times per voice; the likely origin of the PRO-800's Voice Spread.

sources.title: Synth Anatomy launch coverage and Gearspace/KVR threads
sources.note: Behringer's launch text states the PRO-800 includes 'all GliGli modifications'; forum posts say GliGli was involved and that Behringer later made the envelopes snappier.

architecture.signal_path_note: Analogue audio path (two 3340 VCOs, 4-pole filter and VCA per voice). As on the Prophet-600, the envelopes, LFO and vibrato are generated in firmware and sent to the analogue voices as control voltages through a DAC; in the GliGli ancestor this is a 14-bit DAC refreshed at 2 kHz per voice.
architecture.polyphony_mode: 8-voice polyphonic, unison (all 8 on one note, or single-voice unison), or chord mode transposing a held chord
architecture.summary: Eight complete analogue voices, each with two 3340 oscillators (sawtooth, triangle and pulse switchable and mixable; OSC A syncable to OSC B), a noise level, a 24 dB/octave low-pass filter with half or full keyboard tracking, and filter and amplifier ADSR envelopes. Poly-Mod routes the filter envelope and OSC B per voice to OSC A frequency and the filter, which gives the Prophet-600's metallic FM and sync sweeps. One LFO (triangle or pulse on the panel, six shapes through the menu) modulates oscillator frequency, pulse width and the filter, with a separate vibrato. Every panel value is stored in 400 programs, and an additional parameters menu adds envelope curves, velocity and aftertouch depths, pitch bend routing, unison detune, voice spread and glide mode. Arpeggiator, two-bank 400-note real-time sequencer, external clock sync, and autotune of every oscillator and filter.

modules.name: MIDI input
modules.description: Notes, velocity, aftertouch, pitch bend, mod wheel, breath and sustain arrive over MIDI (DIN or USB). No keyboard on this model.

modules.name: Voice assignment and programs
modules.description: Hands notes to the eight voices and holds the program memory. Polyphonic by default; UNISON TRACK switches to unison (all eight voices on one note), chord mode (a held chord transposed by each new note) or single-voice unison, depending on how many keys are held when it is pressed. Priority last, low or high. Also the 400 programs (4 banks of 100), manual and preset modes, autotune, voice select and voice kill.

modules.name: Glide
modules.description: Portamento between notes, by time or by speed.

modules.name: Oscillator A
modules.description: 3340 VCO with sawtooth, triangle and pulse switches that can be combined, pulse width 1 to 99%, and level. Frequency over four octaves in octave, semitone or free steps. Hard-syncs to OSC B. The Poly-Mod destination.

modules.name: Oscillator B
modules.description: 3340 VCO like OSC A, with a FINE control up to a semitone for detuning. A Poly-Mod source and the sync master for OSC A.

modules.name: Noise
modules.description: Noise level into every voice's mixer. Shared by inference, as on the Prophet-600.

modules.name: Voice mixer
modules.description: OSC A level, OSC B level and noise into the filter. Oscillator levels are clean to about 5 and drive the filter into distortion above.

modules.name: Poly-Mod
modules.description: Per-voice modulation from the filter envelope (bipolar amount) and OSC B (unipolar amount), summed and sent to OSC A frequency, the filter, or both. Because each voice has its own, it stays in tune with the notes played: audio-rate FM from OSC B and envelope sync sweeps.

modules.name: Filter
modules.description: 24 dB/octave (4-pole) low-pass with resonance, envelope amount, keyboard tracking off, half or full (full tracks a self-oscillating filter), Poly-Mod and LFO inputs, velocity and aftertouch depths, and the FILTER CV IN.

modules.name: Filter envelope
modules.description: ADSR for the filter, also a Poly-Mod source. Curve selectable fast or slow, exponential or linear. Generated in firmware, not analogue circuitry.

properties.generator: firmware DDS envelope (Electric Druid ENVGEN7 design) at 2 kHz, per voice
properties.source_note: Computed from the GliGli 2.1 source (Electric Druid phase lookup table, 2 kHz update, speed shift 1 for fast and 3 for slow). Behringer is reported to have made the envelopes snappier, so these describe the ancestor, not the PRO-800 exactly. The shortest settings are limited in practice by the 0.5 ms update interval.

modules.name: Amplifier envelope
modules.description: ADSR for the VCA. Curve selectable fast or slow, exponential or linear. Generated in firmware, not analogue circuitry.

properties.generator: firmware DDS envelope (Electric Druid ENVGEN7 design) at 2 kHz, per voice
properties.source_note: Computed from the GliGli 2.1 source (Electric Druid phase lookup table, 2 kHz update, speed shift 1 for fast and 3 for slow). Behringer is reported to have made the envelopes snappier, so these describe the ancestor, not the PRO-800 exactly. The shortest settings are limited in practice by the 0.5 ms update interval.

modules.name: VCA
modules.description: Per-voice amplifier with velocity and aftertouch depths.

modules.name: LFO
modules.description: One LFO for all voices, about 0.08 to 20 Hz with a fast or slow range. The panel switch picks triangle or pulse; the menu then picks triangle, sine or saw in the first position and square, random or noise in the second. INITIAL AMOUNT sets depth without the mod wheel. Destinations: frequency of both oscillators, pulse width of both, the filter. A menu setting limits the oscillator destinations to A, B or both. Optional modulation delay. Generated in firmware at 2 kHz; the vibrato runs at 500 Hz.

modules.name: Vibrato
modules.description: A second, menu-only modulator for pitch vibrato, with speed and amount. The mod wheel can be assigned to it instead of the LFO.

modules.name: Arpeggiator
modules.description: Up, down, up-and-down or up-then-down, by key position, or played or random order. In the GliGli ancestor the up/down mode double-triggers the top and bottom notes, so N notes give an N/4 bar, and REC latches up to 128 notes, adding more while latched. REC or the footswitch latches.

modules.name: Sequencer
modules.description: Two banks of real-time recorded note sequences sharing about 400 notes. Playback speed from 1/4 to 4 times real time, storable.

modules.name: Clock
modules.description: Tempo for the arpeggiator and sequencer: internal BPM, MIDI, USB or the SYNC IN jack, with subdivision and PPQN settings.

modules.name: Output
modules.description: Voices summed, master volume, master tune; rear 1/4-inch output, top 1/8-inch output and phones.

behaviours.name: Eight true voices
behaviours.rule: Every module marked per_voice exists eight times with shared settings and independent state. Unlike the Poly D, each voice has its own filter, VCA and envelopes, so this is true polyphony. LFO, vibrato and noise are shared.

behaviours.name: Keyboard modes from one switch
behaviours.rule: UNISON TRACK does three things depending on what is held when it is pressed: nothing held gives unison (all eight voices on one note, detuned by the Unison/Spread Detune setting); one key held gives single-voice unison, a monophonic synth; a chord held gives chord mode, where that chord is transposed by every new note and saved with the preset. The sustain pedal can also set the chord while in unison.

behaviours.name: Voice priority
behaviours.rule: Last: new notes always play and the oldest are stolen. Low or High: only the lowest or highest notes play, and in unison or chord modes these are legato.

behaviours.name: Poly-Mod
behaviours.rule: Each voice's filter envelope (bipolar) and OSC B (unipolar) are summed and sent to OSC A frequency, the filter, or both. With OSC B at audio rate this is per-voice FM that stays in tune with each note; with SYNC on and the filter envelope into FREQ A it is the classic Prophet sync sweep.

behaviours.name: Oscillator level drives the filter
behaviours.rule: The oscillator LEVEL controls are clean up to about 5; above that the filter input is progressively overdriven.

behaviours.name: LFO shapes in two groups
behaviours.rule: The panel SHAPE switch picks a group and the menu picks the shape within it: triangle, sine or saw in the triangle position; square, random or noise in the pulse position. The LFO target setting restricts FREQ A-B and PW A-B to OSC A, OSC B or both.

behaviours.name: Programs and manual mode
behaviours.rule: 400 programs in banks A to D of 100. In preset mode the sound is the stored program and the PRESET LED blinks once anything is edited. Manual mode (PERF twice, display P800) makes the sound follow the panel. REC then two digits stores.

behaviours.name: Autotune
behaviours.rule: At power-up and on TUNE, every oscillator and filter in all eight voices is calibrated (display A1 to A8, b1 to b8, F1 to F8), taking about 20 seconds with the output muted. A long press does a quicker temperature correction. Precision is set from 0.5 to 2 cents. Expect to retune in the first 30 minutes.

behaviours.name: Sequencer
behaviours.rule: Real-time recording into two banks sharing about 400 notes; recording starts on the first key and ends with REC or the footswitch. If the limit is passed the earliest notes are lost, and recording into one bank steals notes from the other. Playback at 1/4 to 4 times, with 1:1 left of centre on VALUE; press REC during playback to store the speed.

behaviours.name: Arpeggiator
behaviours.rule: ARP UP-DN arpeggiates by key position (up, down, up and down, up then down); ARP ASSIGN by played or random order. REC or the footswitch latches. Holding notes then pressing ARP UP-DN drones them without arpeggiation.

behaviours.name: Performance controllers
behaviours.rule: Aftertouch, pitch bend and the mod wheel act on parameters rather than as signals: aftertouch scales VCA level, cutoff and LFO depth by their menu amounts; pitch bend goes to pitch, cutoff or volume over 0 to 24 semitones; the mod wheel scales the LFO or the vibrato over one of four ranges. Recorded as parameters, not connections.

behaviours.name: Envelope shapes
behaviours.rule: Each envelope has a menu shape: fast or slow range, exponential or linear curve. No times are given for any setting.

behaviours.name: Firmware-generated modulation
behaviours.rule: The audio path is analogue but the envelopes, LFO and vibrato are computed by the microcontroller and written to each voice as control voltages, as on the original Prophet-600. In the GliGli ancestor this happens 2,000 times a second per voice through a 14-bit DAC. This is why envelope curve and speed are menu choices, why Voice Spread can vary envelope times per voice, and why firmware updates have changed how the envelopes feel.
behaviours.note: From the GliGli manual and source; Behringer does not describe its implementation.

behaviours.name: Knob resolution
behaviours.rule: In the GliGli ancestor every knob is read at more than 8 bits for smooth changes, though values are displayed as 0 to 255. Scratchy pots are audible as wavering at this resolution, especially pulse width and cutoff with high resonance.

transmits: cc and program change when enabled

channel.set_by: global settings (Rx and Tx separately), or the rear DIP switches when set to Dipswitch

midi.cc_resolution: Continuous parameters take a coarse CC (8 to 42) and a fine CC (80 to 117) for 14-bit resolution (0 to 16383), or coarse alone for 0 to 127. Stepped parameters (48 to 79) divide 0 to 127 into equal zones, one per choice; for example Unison is off for 0 to 63 and on for 64 to 127. From the GliGli MIDI implementation, which the PRO-800 follows with its own CC numbers.
midi.nrpn: Data entry, increment and decrement CCs listed; the NRPN parameter numbers are not given.
midi.sysex: Preset dump only; format not given.

usb.os: Windows 7 or higher, Mac OS X 10.11.6 or higher

midi.note: The GliGli firmware receives CCs in preset mode only; whether the PRO-800 keeps that restriction is not stated. Behringer's CC numbers differ from GliGli's (for example OSC A frequency is 8 here, 16 in GliGli).

source_inconsistencies: The English control list is out of order and several numbers carry the wrong description (for example 22 and 23 share one line covering FINE and FIL ENV, and 59 is labelled MIDI IN on the rear while the panel's MIDI IN is on the top).
LFO range: 'about 0.25 to 20 Hz' in item 29, 0.08 to 20 Hz in the specifications.
The specifications list LFO shape as triangle or pulse; the menu offers six shapes.
SYNC CLOCK lists PPQN of 24, 48, 96 and 192; the global setting and the specifications list 1 PPS, 2, 4, 24 and 48.
ENVELOPE AMOUNT is marked -5 to +5 on the panel and 0 to 10 in the specifications; the guide says 0 is no effect.
CC 48 and 49 are both printed as 'OSC A Saw'; 49 is read as OSC A triangle. CCs 52 and 53 print 'OSB B'. CC 79's hex is printed 'AF' for 4F.
The LFO shape instructions tell you to 'Enter Pref mode' for the square group; read as PERF.
The button is labelled ARP UP-DN in the controls and ARP UP-ON in the specifications.
The guide's tune routine, keyboard modes and LFO instructions are copied from the GliGli manual; its 'Enter Pref mode' is a garbling of the GliGli instruction to light the 'to tape' button.
LFO range: the GliGli ancestor spans about 0.017 to 62.5 Hz; the PRO-800 guide gives 0.08 to 20 Hz.
Pitch bend range: GliGli offers a third, a fifth or an octave; the PRO-800 offers 0 to 24 semitones.

modelling_gaps.detail: Envelope stage times are now estimated from the GliGli source (about 0.5 ms to 37 s fast, to 175 s slow, exponential taper), but Behringer has altered the envelopes since. Cutoff range and resonance law remain unknown; the Prophet-600 used a Curtis 4-pole filter.
Voice Spread deliberately varies voices; inherent voice-to-voice tolerance after autotune is not documented.
Poly-Mod amounts have no stated scaling in semitones or octaves at full travel.

Confirmed by Behringer's launch text and by text copied into the guide. The open-source code gives exact envelope, LFO and MIDI behaviour for the ancestor; the menu items the GliGli 2.0 release lacks (keyboard tracking reference note, voice spread, glide mode, aftertouch amounts, 0 to 24 semitone bend) come from Imogen's later fork or from Behringer.
